title: Should the US publicly subsidize film?

commenti.body: I think that we aren't at that point yet. Maybe in the future we will be with how many theaters are closing down and how most people seen to prefer streaming. But I think right now movies make enough money that this isn't a problem. Plus don't studios usually film in cities that give them the most tax brakes, a program set up for the government, so  you could say that filmmaking is already at least partially subsidized.

Film as an *industry* isn't dying, film as an *art form* is imo*.* And yes films are subsidized through tax credits, but any film that shoots in the area gets the tax credit. The function of the credit is not to subsidize films that have artistic merit, it's to generate economic activity in the area. On the other hand the point of the fund would be to subsidize films with artistic merit.
